Generated Narrative
Your compromise lands, not cleanly, but heavily enough that no one immediately rejects it. Mayor Elric exhales through his nose and looks from Mitch to Arlen, then to the gathered townsfolk. “A formal inquiry,” he says, voice rough but public. “Full records. Witness statements. Watch reports. Temple accounts. No more quiet handling.” Captain Varr’s jaw tightens, but he gives a curt nod. “The watch will secure the records.” Arlen stands very still near the edge of the lanternlight. The crowd’s attention turns on him like a blade. For a moment, it looks as though he might argue, vanish, or lash out with some cutting word. Instead, he lowers his gaze. “No further alterations,” Arlen says. “No veils. No omissions. Not without consent.” The words stir the square more than they soothe it. A few people mutter. Someone spits onto the cobbles. Jorin, unusually silent, watches the wizard with narrowed eyes. Mitch looks smaller than he did a moment ago. When Serah’s name is spoken, his expression flickers between shame and desperate hope. He does not look saved. He looks like a man being handed one rope while still standing in deep water. Mayor Elric turns to him. “You’ll go to the Temple of the Tide. Tonight.” Mitch nods once. The agreement holds, but barely. It hangs over the square like a lantern in wind: Arlen restrained, Mitch sent for treatment, the mayor bound to an inquiry in front of witnesses. No one cheers. No one looks satisfied. But for the first time tonight, the shouting has stopped.
Raw LLM Output (last attempt)
Thoughts: Show the compromise taking hold, but keep the mood tense and unresolved.

Narrative: Your compromise lands, not cleanly, but heavily enough that no one immediately rejects it.

Mayor Elric exhales through his nose and looks from Mitch to Arlen, then to the gathered townsfolk. “A formal inquiry,” he says, voice rough but public. “Full records. Witness statements. Watch reports. Temple accounts. No more quiet handling.”

Captain Varr’s jaw tightens, but he gives a curt nod. “The watch will secure the records.”

Arlen stands very still near the edge of the lanternlight. The crowd’s attention turns on him like a blade. For a moment, it looks as though he might argue, vanish, or lash out with some cutting word. Instead, he lowers his gaze.

“No further alterations,” Arlen says. “No veils. No omissions. Not without consent.”

The words stir the square more than they soothe it. A few people mutter. Someone spits onto the cobbles. Jorin, unusually silent, watches the wizard with narrowed eyes.

Mitch looks smaller than he did a moment ago. When Serah’s name is spoken, his expression flickers between shame and desperate hope. He does not look saved. He looks like a man being handed one rope while still standing in deep water.

Mayor Elric turns to him. “You’ll go to the Temple of the Tide. Tonight.”

Mitch nods once.

The agreement holds, but barely. It hangs over the square like a lantern in wind: Arlen restrained, Mitch sent for treatment, the mayor bound to an inquiry in front of witnesses. No one cheers. No one looks satisfied.

But for the first time tonight, the shouting has stopped.
